data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Confidence is self-reported and strategically manipulable; residual structure in errors is behavioral.","Training can teach 'be unsure when the checklist is silent,' producing good calibration without genuine reliability."],"overturn_conditions":["The panel is trained to report low confidence on checklist-silent cases, artifactually passing calibration without genuine knowledge.","Confidence reports are not collected or not trustworthy."],"shared_structure":["Confidence calibration is a classic test of metacognitive access to the decision basis; miscalibration on an unmodeled subspace reveals that confidence is driven by the proxy (checklist completeness), not the target (correctness)."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_005","SRC_006"],"transfer_claims":["Use confidence calibration on the checklist-irrelevant subset as a litmus test: good calibration implies genuine access to the decision basis; poor calibration implies compliance-only."]},"claim":"Within a single evaluation, genuine reliability is distinguished from compliance-tracking by the correlation between panel confidence and correctness on the checklist-irrelevant subset: a genuinely reliable panel should be appropriately calibrated (confidence tracks correctness) even on cases where the checklist gives no guidance, whereas a compliance-tracking panel will be uniformly confident whenever the checklist is complete, independent of whether the checklist-irrelevant cue points the other way.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the task has no checklist-irrelevant, outcome-relevant cues, the subset is empty and the test is void.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the panel is trained to be uncertain when the checklist is silent, the overconfidence signature may vanish without genuine cue-knowledge.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert is equally overconfident, the contrast is lost.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Reliability entails a metacognitive alignment between confidence and accuracy. A compliance-only process produces confidence from checklist completeness ('I checked every box'), which is decoupled from checklist-irrelevant, outcome-relevant signals. Hence on cases where the checklist is silent but an outcome-relevant cue exists, the compliance panel will be overconfident and wrong, producing a miscalibration signature: high confidence, low accuracy, on the checklist-irrelevant subset. A genuinely reliable process would show lower confidence or different accuracy on that subset.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
